bull.probability_evidence: Conviction is capped at 4/5 (not 5) specifically because 'AI-driven pricing pressure in DIY tax and the FY2027 reset make the timing of a re-rating uncertain' (evaluation.md Decision JSON, rationale), which bounds the bull weight to a minority 25% despite 'big bets' at 30% of revenue each growing >30% (Investor Day 2026 transcript, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/intu/transcripts/612260-investor-day-2026/).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table: re-pricing the bull case's peer-median re-rating across the three main multiples gives divergent targets — P/E 17.3x->22.0x: 289.81*(22.0/17.3)=368.68; EV/EBITDA 11.5x->14.6x: 289.81*(14.6/11.5)=367.86; P/FCF 8.9x->16.8x: 289.81*(16.8/8.9)=547.03 (INTU's P/FCF sits far further below the peer median than its P/E or EV/EBITDA, because FCF conversion is 190% of net income). Half the spread (547.03-367.86)/2=89.59 / target 368 = 0.243; within residual_vol blended 0.4433 (mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended).

base.probability_evidence: Management itself guided this path at the September 17, 2026 Investor Day ('Fiscal 2027 is a reset year... targeting 9%-10% revenue growth', https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/intu/transcripts/612260-investor-day-2026/) and reaffirmed it in the FY27 guidance headline (Q1 EPS $2.44-$2.48 vs consensus $2.72, fact sheet News & sentiment), making the guided reset the modal (50%) outcome rather than a tail.

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table: re-pricing the base case's 5y-minimum re-rating across the three main multiples: P/E 17.3x->18.9x: 289.81*(18.9/17.3)=316.68; EV/EBITDA 11.5x->12.6x: 289.81*(12.6/11.5)=317.65; P/FCF 8.9x->10.0x: 289.81*(10.0/8.9)=325.60 (matches the evaluation's stated basis). Half the spread (325.60-316.68)/2=4.46 / target 326 = 0.014; within residual_vol blended 0.4433 (mc-inputs.json).

bear.probability_evidence: Weighed down to 25% by offsetting factors: the margin-compression risk is real ('management itself says price is the top reason DIY tax customers leave', evaluation.md Bear case) but short interest is only 2.69% of float and fell 11.8% month-on-month, and Piotroski F is 7 (fact sheet Other/News & sentiment tables), arguing against a high-probability bear outcome.

jumps.name: Quarterly earnings/guidance miss (FY2027 reset)
jumps.reason: Management guided Q1 FY27 EPS $2.44-$2.48 and FY27 EPS $22.88-$23.12, both below consensus ($2.72 / $24.18), and called FY2027 a slower 'reset year' at the Sept 17, 2026 Investor Day — the next report (Nov 19, 2026) is the first test of that guidance.
jumps.cite: Fact sheet News & sentiment: 'Intuit sees Q1 EPS $2.44-$2.48, consensus $2.72' and 'Intuit sees FY27 EPS $22.88-$23.12, consensus $24.18' (2026-09-17, TheFly); note.md section 2, 'guided fiscal 2027 to a slower reset year'.

annual_probability.cite: Of 20 quarterly earnings weeks in mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks (Q1 2022-Q4 2026), only 1 (Q3 2026, -0.1859) reached this magnitude (>=15%): ~5% per-quarter base rate; probability of at least one such quarter within a year = 1-(0.95)^4 ~= 0.19.

impact.cite: Matches the analogue: the Q3 2026 earnings week (2026-05-18), the single largest weekly move in the regression history (mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks, event='Q3 2026').

jumps.name: AI-native disruption / price-driven DIY tax churn disclosed at Investor Day
jumps.reason: Management's own stated top reason for DIY tax customer churn is price (not AI-native competitors), but the market is pricing a durable impairment of the tax/bookkeeping franchise from AI-native entrants; a fresh disclosure of worsening competitive dynamics (most likely at the annual Investor Day) could re-price this discretely.
jumps.cite: evaluation.md Bear case: 'AI-native tools could commoditise DIY tax and small-business bookkeeping, and management itself says price is the top reason DIY tax customers leave'; note.md section 2, 'management said the top reason DIY tax customers left was price' (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/intu/transcripts/612260-investor-day-2026/).

annual_probability.cite: mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks lists one Investor Day per year (2022-2026), but none produced a move anywhere near this magnitude (range -0.0572 to +0.0648) -- a -0.30 structural shock is a tail case versus the routine annual event, estimated at roughly 1-in-6-7 years (~0.15).

impact.cite: No historical analogue isolates a competitive-disruption shock distinct from scheduled earnings/investor-day moves already captured by the Investor Day 2026 week (-0.0572, already reflected in the current price); capped at [montecarlo].max_jump_impact_assumed = 0.30 per the assumption rule for risks without an analogue.

jumps.assumption: No historical analogue for a standalone structural AI-competition impairment shock exists in the jump-analogue table; impact set at the 0.30 cap per [montecarlo].max_jump_impact_assumed rather than estimated from a specific week.

technical_tilt.cite: Fact sheet Price table: 3-month momentum +6.5% (2026-07-06->2026-10-06) outperforms SPY's +3.7% by +2.8pp, RSI(14) is 43.1 (not overbought), with recent swing lows (322.57, 309.80, 262.32) suggesting a base forming even as the stock remains 25.7%/10.2% below its 200/50-day MAs — a modest positive 3-month tilt, held well inside the ±0.02 cap given the still-deep longer-term downtrend.
